As of October 10, the biggest Warren Buffett story is not a new investment personally announced by the 96 year old investor, but the formal end of his Berkshire Hathaway era. Bloomberg and CNBC report that Buffett stepped down as chief executive at the end of 2025 and became chairman emeritus in September, with Greg Abel running the company and Buffett’s son Howard becoming chairman. Buffett remains on Berkshire’s board, but the succession that investors watched for decades is now history. Berkshire is also making a conspicuous post Buffett move in housing. Realtor.com reports that the company increased its Lennar stake by 94 percent during the third quarter, bringing ownership to roughly 11 percent. The latest Securities and Exchange Commission filing, reviewed by International Business Times, shows purchases of more than 2.4 million Class A shares and additional Class B shares worth about 192.6 million dollars on October 1 and 2. Warren Buffett is still listed as a reporting person, but available reporting attributes the strategy to Abel rather than to a new Buffett directive. Lennar’s weaker outlook and a short seller’s report make the timing especially notable, although any claim that Buffett personally ordered the purchases is unconfirmed. The broader biographical significance is clear. Fortune reports that Berkshire has already acquired Taylor Morrison for about 6.8 billion dollars, while the Lennar investment expands a homebuilding strategy that could make Berkshire one of America’s largest site built housing operators. That is a meaningful departure in emphasis under Abel, even if the long term investment style remains recognizably Berkshire. Forbes estimates Buffett’s fortune at roughly 142 billion dollars, placing him around tenth among the world’s richest people. Other financial reporting puts the figure near 143 billion and says his wealth has fallen about 8.3 billion dollars this year, illustrating how closely his fortune remains tied to Berkshire’s share price. The most personal headline comes from the Wall Street Journal, as relayed by Fortune. Friends say Buffett now spends many evenings watching YouTube, including old commercials, Glenn Close clips, and Uzbekistani talent shows. Buffett declined to comment, so the details are attributed to friends rather than confirmed by him. Finally, the so called Buffett Indicator is again making headlines because stock market values compared with the economy are at record levels. Commentators are revisiting Buffett’s old warnings about speculation, but no reliable report says he has issued a new crash forecast. Thank you for listening. Please subscribe so you never miss a Warren Buffett update, and search Biography Flash for more great biographies. Thanks for listening. This has been a Quiet Please production.
